assessment.nobel_worthiness: Chemically induced proximity that hijacks the ubiquitin-proteasome system to destroy proteins, including ones with no druggable pocket, is a molecular design principle that has changed what chemists and clinicians can target. Heterobifunctional PROTACs and monovalent molecular glues (thalidomide-class degraders) have opened a new modality and a broad toolkit for chemical biology.
assessment.attribution: The PROTAC concept and first proof of principle trace to Crews and Deshaies; Ciulli supplied the structure-guided VHL ligands and ternary-complex rationale that made the approach general. The molecular-glue branch (Handa, Ito, Gray and others) is also strong, so any three-person split leaves out a major contributor.
assessment.maturity: Clinical degraders are in late-stage trials and the mechanistic literature is large and independently confirmed, though no PROTAC drug is approved yet. Recognition is on the early side of timely but defensible given the breadth of adoption.
uncertainties: Whether PROTACs and molecular glues should be recognized together or only one branch
Clinical validation is incomplete, with no approved PROTAC
Credit split between concept originators and the later glue-degrader discoveries

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Massively parallel sequencing, built on chemistry (reversible terminators, clonal amplification on surfaces, pyrosequencing), has reshaped biology and medicine and is a clear case of a chemical method changing what researchers and clinicians can do. Impact is enormous and sustained.
assessment.attribution: Balasubramanian and Klenerman developed the single-molecule array and reversible-terminator chemistry behind the dominant Solexa/Illumina platform. Rothberg commercialized pyrosequencing in picoliter wells (454), the first commercial next-generation platform. Pascal Mayer and Jingyue Ju also have credible claims, so credit allocation is contestable.
assessment.maturity: Fully mature: two decades of use, many independent platforms and routine clinical application. Timing is not an issue.
uncertainties: Whether the prize would be seen as chemistry rather than biology or medicine
Competing contributions from Mayer and Ju, and from earlier sequencing-chemistry work
Rothberg's contribution is commercialization-driven, which could weigh against him

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Liquid-liquid phase separation as an organizing principle of the cell brought physical chemistry (polymer physics, multivalency) to cell biology and created a new framework for membraneless organelles, disease-linked aggregation and drug partitioning. The conceptual novelty is high, and the connection to peptide and protein self-assembly is close to my own work.
assessment.attribution: Brangwynne and Hyman established P granules as liquid droplets; Rosen demonstrated multivalent-interaction-driven phase separation in reconstituted systems. Pappu and Mittag supplied sequence-encoded physical theory and grammar. A three-person limit forces difficult choices.
assessment.maturity: The field is young and contested: debate continues on the physiological relevance of condensates versus in vitro droplets, and therapeutic payoff is not yet shown. Rank reflects an important idea whose interpretation is still evolving.
uncertainties: Disagreement on in vivo physiological significance of condensates
Prize category fit (biology/medicine versus chemistry)
Unresolved credit among five strong contributors

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Nanopore reading of single nucleic-acid molecules is a molecular-recognition and sensing technology, close to my field of biosensing, that grew from protein-pore engineering and ion-current detection into long-read sequencing and single-molecule analytics. It changed what field and clinical laboratories can do.
assessment.attribution: Deamer, Branton and Akeson proposed and demonstrated the idea of threading polynucleotides; Kasianowicz showed the first detection; Bayley engineered alpha-hemolysin and later contributed to the enabling pore chemistry. Branton's death (as I recall, 2020) removes him from consideration; the remaining credit among Bayley, Deamer, Akeson and Kasianowicz is contested.
assessment.maturity: Technology is commercial and widely independently validated (long reads, portable sequencing). Mature, though some accuracy limits remain.
uncertainties: Allocation of credit among Kasianowicz, Bayley, Deamer and Akeson
Status of Branton (I believe deceased, not verified)
Overlap with the sequencing candidate and partly with Medicine/Physiology

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Lipid nanoparticles with ionizable lipids provided the delivery chemistry that makes nucleic-acid drugs (siRNA, mRNA vaccines) work in patients. This is an example of a chemical design principle (pKa-tuned lipids, self-assembly) that enabled a medical revolution.
assessment.attribution: The Vancouver group (Cullis, Hope, Madden) developed the formulation and ionizable-lipid principles; MacLachlan, Anderson and Langer contributed lipid design and lipidoid discovery. Credit is spread across academia and industry and patent disputes complicate an assessment.
assessment.maturity: Clinically validated at global scale and mature. Recognition of the mRNA vaccine itself in Medicine 2023 may reduce urgency, but delivery chemistry was not part of that citation.
uncertainties: Credit dispersed across several groups and companies
Possible perception that the topic is already covered by the 2023 Medicine prize
My facts on who made decisive ionizable-lipid advances are from general knowledge

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Shokat's work on covalent targeting of the KRAS G12C pocket and analog-sensitive kinase chemical genetics showed that a long-undruggable oncogene could be drugged by molecular design, directly altering clinical practice. Strong example of a chemical tool translating to therapy.
assessment.attribution: Credit is clearly centered on one laureate for the KRAS G12C covalent strategy and for chemical genetics of kinases. Subsequent drug development (sotorasib, adagrasib) was done by companies building on his tethering approach.
assessment.maturity: Approved drugs exist and the concept is independently confirmed, but long-term benefit is still being assessed due to resistance and modest durability.
uncertainties: Whether resistance limits long-term significance
A single-laureate prize may be seen as narrow versus the broader covalent-drug field
Combination of two discoveries (kinase chemical genetics and KRAS) in one candidate

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Expanding the genetic code with orthogonal tRNA/synthetase pairs lets chemists install designed non-canonical amino acids into proteins in living cells, a general route to protein engineering, biomaterials, and chemical biology. This is a molecular design platform with wide use.
assessment.attribution: Schultz made the foundational demonstration in E. coli and then eukaryotes with Wang; Chin extended the approach to multiple, quadruplet and genomically recoded systems. Mehl and Yokoyama have significant contributions, so the three-person allocation is debatable.
assessment.maturity: Widely adopted and independently confirmed for two decades; therapeutic applications (e.g., antibody-drug conjugates) are emerging. Mature and arguably overdue.
uncertainties: Whether Schultz alone or the broader field is preferred
Credit among Wang, Mehl, Yokoyama and Chin
Application impact beyond research tools is still developing

assessment.nobel_worthiness: DNA origami turned nucleic acids into programmable building material for nanoscale structures, with applications in biosensing, plasmonic assembly and drug delivery. It is a clear molecular design principle for precise control of assembly, though the field's greatest practical applications are still in development.
assessment.attribution: Rothemund introduced scaffolded origami; Yan, Shih and Yin extended it to 3D structures and applications; Winfree contributed algorithmic self-assembly. Seeman's foundational structural DNA nanotechnology is not on the credited list (and he died in 2021, as I recall), which weakens a configuration without him.
assessment.maturity: Reproducible and widely used, but the transition from demonstrations to functional technologies is less advanced; recognition could be seen as premature or as needing Seeman-era context.
uncertainties: Absence of Seeman from the supplied credit
Practical impact beyond research tools is limited so far
Division among Rothemund, Yan, Shih, Yin and Winfree
